content: The following are professional interpretations of the provided references: 1. Ferrand RA and colleagues developed an algorithm at the primary care level to identify adolescents living with HIV who are at risk of long-term survival due to mother-to-child transmission. This study was published in Tropical Medicine and International Health in 2011. 2. Denison J and colleagues explored the influence of social relationships on adolescents' decisions regarding HIV counseling and testing in Zambia. This research was documented by the Population Council in 2006. 3. Ho WW and colleagues examined the complexities surrounding HIV consent among adolescents, highlighting ethical and practical challenges. Their findings were published in Clinical Pediatrics in 2005. 4. Klein JD and colleagues analyzed access to medical care for adolescents, focusing on data from the 1997 Commonwealth Fund Survey on the health of adolescent girls. This study appeared in the Journal of Adolescent Health in 1999. 5. 6. Their findings were published in PLoS One in 2012. 7. Sherman BF and colleagues studied the psychological and disease progression consequences for children who disclose their HIV status to friends. This research was published in Psychosomatic Medicine in 2000. 8. Their findings were published in the Journal of Adolescent Health in 2012. 9. This study was published in AIDS Patient Care and STDs in 2007. 10. Sayles JN and colleagues explored how the inability to take medications openly at home may contribute to gender disparities in the use of highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART). Their findings were published in the Journal of Women’s Health in 2006. 11. Beyene KA and colleagues assessed adherence to HAART and its determinants in selected hospitals in southern and central Ethiopia. This study was published in Pharmacoepidemiology and Drug Safety in 2009. 12. Ochieng-Ooko V and colleagues investigated the influence of gender on loss to follow-up in a large HIV treatment program in western Kenya. Their findings were published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2010. 13. Rotheram-Borus MJ and colleagues highlighted the benefits of family and social relationships for Thai parents living with HIV. This study was published in Prevention Science in 2010. 14. Abaynew Y, Deribew A, and Deribe K identified factors associated with late presentation to HIV/AIDS care in South Wollo Zone, Ethiopia. Their case-control study was published in AIDS Research and Therapy in 2011. 15. This study was published in AIDS Care in 2011. 16. Hatcher AM and colleagues identified predictors of linkage to care following community-based HIV counseling and testing in rural Kenya. Their findings were published in AIDS and Behavior in 2012. 17. This research was published in AIDS Care in 2006. 18. This study was published in Psychosomatic Medicine in 2007. 19. This was part of the Kericho IRIS study presented at the 19th International AIDS Conference in 2012. 20. Peltzer K and Mlambo G identified factors influencing HIV viral testing of infants in the context of mother-to-child transmission. Their findings were published in Acta Paediatrica in 2010. 21. Peltzer K, Sikwane E, and Majaja M examined factors associated with adherence to short-course antiretroviral prophylaxis for PMTCT in South Africa. This study was published in Acta Paediatrica in 2011. 22. This study was published in AIDS and Behavior in 2013. 23. Sigxashe TA and colleagues explored attitudes toward disclosing HIV status to sexual partners. Their findings were published in the South African Medical Journal in 2001. 24. This research was published in AIDS Care in 2003. 25. Their findings were published in AIDS in 2005. 26. This study was published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2009. 27. Their findings were published in AIDS Care in 2011. 28. This research was published in the African Journal of Reproductive Health in 2012. 29. This study was published in the Journal of Community & Applied Social Psychology in 2000. 30. Kilewo C and colleagues shared experiences from a study on HIV counseling and testing of pregnant women in sub-Saharan Africa for the prevention of mother-to-child transmission. Their findings were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2001. 31. This study was published in the East African Journal of Public Health in 2010. 32. 33. Rotheram-Borus MJ and colleagues developed an intervention for parents with AIDS and their adolescent children. This study was published in the American Journal of Public Health in 2001. 34. Serovich JM and colleagues piloted an intervention to assist men who have sex with men in disclosing their serostatus to family members. This study was published in AIDS and Behavior in 2011. 35. Mundell JP and colleagues evaluated the impact of structured support groups for pregnant South African women recently diagnosed as HIV-positive. This study was published in Women’s Health in 2011. 36. Otis J and colleagues assessed the effects of an empowerment program on women living with HIV in Mali regarding their decisions to disclose their HIV status. This was presented at the 19th International AIDS Conference in 2012. 37. This study was published in the Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology in 2011. 38. This study was published in AIDS in 2005. 39. Serovich JM and colleagues piloted an intervention to assist men who have sex with men in disclosing their serostatus to casual sexual partners. This study was published in AIDS Education and Prevention in 2009. 40. Smith-Fawzi MC and colleagues implemented a psychosocial support intervention for HIV-affected families in Haiti, with implications for programs and policies for orphans and vulnerable children. This study was published in Social Science & Medicine in 2012. 41. Rotheram-Borus MJ and colleagues presented findings on the Masihambisane intervention, which involved HIV-positive peer community health workers supporting South African mothers living with HIV. This was presented at the 2012 International AIDS Conference. 42. This study was published in AIDS and Behavior in 2010. 43. Dewo Z and colleagues presented findings on strengthening treatment, care, and support for people living with HIV through community-based treatment services at the 19th International AIDS Conference in 2012. 44. This study was published in AIDS Patient Care and STDs in 2009. 45. Olley BO evaluated the impact of psycho-education on improving well-being among voluntary counseling and testing seekers in Nigeria. This study was published in AIDS Care in 2006. 46. Patterson TL, Shaw WS, and Semple SJ conducted a randomized controlled trial to reduce the sexual risk behaviors of HIV-positive individuals. This study was published in Annals of Behavioral Medicine in 2003. 47. This study was published in AIDS Care in 2009. 48. The WHO provided guidance on couples HIV testing and counseling, including ART for treatment and prevention in serodiscordant couples, in 2012. 49. Kabore I and colleagues evaluated the effect of community-based support services on clinical efficacy and health-related quality of life in HIV/AIDS patients in sub-Saharan Africa. This study was published in AIDS Patient Care and STDs in 2010. 50. Fatti G and colleagues reported improved survival and ART outcomes in adults receiving community-based adherence support in South Africa. This study was published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2012. 51. Grimwood A and colleagues found that community adherence support improved program retention in children on ART in South Africa. This study was published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2012. 52. Chang LW and colleagues evaluated the impact of peer health workers on AIDS care in Rakai, Uganda, through a cluster-randomized trial. This study was published in PLoS One in 2010. 53. Chang LW and colleagues assessed the impact of an mHealth intervention for peer health workers on AIDS care in rural Uganda. This study was published in AIDS and Behavior in 2011. 54. Selke HM and colleagues evaluated the clinical outcomes of a community-based program in Kenya that shifted antiretroviral delivery from healthcare workers to persons living with HIV/AIDS. This study was published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2010. 55. Simoni JM and colleagues conducted a randomized controlled trial to promote antiretroviral therapy adherence using peer support and pager messaging in Seattle. This study was published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2009. 56. Taiwo BO and colleagues assessed the virologic and adherence benefits of patient-selected HIV treatment partners in a resource-limited setting. This study was published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2010. 57. Futterman D and colleagues conducted a pilot study combining a cognitive-behavioral intervention and mentor mothers with PMTCT services in South Africa. This study was published in AIDS Care in 2010. 58. Talisuna-Alamo S and colleagues found that socioeconomic support reduced non-retention in a community-based ART program in Uganda. This study was published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2012. 59. Altice FL and colleagues demonstrated the superiority of directly administered ART over self-administered therapy among HIV-infected drug users. This study was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2007. 60. Pearson CR and colleagues conducted a randomized control trial of peer-delivered, modified directly observed therapy for HAART in Mozambique. This study was published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2007. 61. Macalino GE and colleagues evaluated the impact of community-based directly observed therapy as an adherence intervention for HAART among substance users. This study was published in AIDS in 2007. 62. Igumbor JO and colleagues assessed the impact of a community-based adherence support program on ART outcomes in South Africa. This study was published in AIDS Care in 2011. 63. Achieng L and colleagues compared facilitators of retention in care and adherence to ART at an HIV treatment center in Kenya. This study was published in PLoS One in 2012. 64. Bekker LG and colleagues reported on the rapid scale-up of a community-based HIV treatment service in South Africa over three consecutive years. This study was published in the South African Medical Journal in 2006. 65. Chang LW and colleagues evaluated the two-year virologic outcomes of a peer health worker and nurse-staffed community-based program in Uganda. This study was published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2009. 66. Kipp W and colleagues reported on the outcomes of a community-based ART program for HIV-1 infection in western Uganda. This study was published in Current HIV Research in 2010. 67. Kipp W and colleagues compared ART outcomes between community-based and hospital-based cohorts of HIV patients in rural Uganda. This study was published in BMC International Health and Human Rights in 2011. 68. Nglazi MD and colleagues analyzed changes in programmatic outcomes during seven years of scale-up at a community-based ART service in South Africa. This study was published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2011. 69. Nglazi MD and colleagues evaluated treatment outcomes in HIV-infected adolescents attending a community-based ART clinic in South Africa. This study was published in BMC Infectious Diseases in 2012. 70. Rich ML and colleagues reported excellent clinical outcomes and high retention in care among adults in a community-based HIV treatment program in rural Rwanda. This study was published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2012. 71. Stubbs BA and colleagues examined the role of treatment partners in adherence to HAART in central Mozambique. This study was published in AIDS Care in 2009. 72. Nan da P and colleagues evaluated the effectiveness of WHO tools in improving the quality of health services provided to female clients in India. This study was published by the WHO in 2012. 73. Robling M and colleagues assessed the impact of the Talking Diabetes consulting skills intervention on glycemic control and quality of life in children with type 1 diabetes. This study was published in the British Medical Journal in 2012. 74. Gregory J and colleagues developed and evaluated a psychosocial intervention for children and teenagers with diabetes. This study was published in Health Technology Assessment in 2011. 75. Lozano P and colleagues conducted a multisite randomized trial on the effects of physician education and organizational change in chronic asthma care. This study was published in the Archives of Pediatrics & Adolescent Medicine in 2004. 76. Shroufi A and colleagues demonstrated that HIV-infected adolescents in southern Africa can achieve good treatment outcomes. This study was published in AIDS in 2013. 77. Dewing S and colleagues evaluated the effectiveness of lay counselors in providing ARV adherence support in South Africa. This study was published in AIDS and Behavior in 2012. 78. Fisher JD and colleagues found that clinician-delivered interventions during routine clinical care reduced unprotected sexual behavior among HIV-infected patients. This study was published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2006. 79. Dewing S and colleagues assessed the fidelity of lay counselors to evidence-based interventions for promoting ARV adherence in South Africa. This manuscript was submitted for publication. 80. Dewing S and colleagues evaluated the ability of lay counselors to deliver counseling for behavior change. This manuscript was submitted for publication. 81. Dewing S and colleagues conducted a cluster randomized controlled trial to improve the counseling skills of lay counselors in ARV adherence settings in South Africa. This manuscript is in preparation. 82. Lewin SA and colleagues reviewed the role of lay health workers in primary and community healthcare for maternal and child health and infectious disease management. This study was published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2010. 83. Wong CF and colleagues examined harassment, discrimination, violence, and illicit drug use among young men who have sex with men. This study was published in AIDS Education and Prevention in 2010. 84. Hurt CB and colleagues found that sex with older partners is associated with primary HIV infection among men who have sex with men in North Carolina. This study was published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2010. 85. Koblin BA and colleagues identified risk factors for HIV infection among men who have sex with men. This study was published in AIDS in 2006. 86. The UNAIDS Inter-Agency Task Team on Education emphasized the importance of HIV and AIDS treatment education as a critical component of universal access to prevention, treatment, and care. This report was published by UNESCO in 2006. 87. Ferrand RA and colleagues developed a primary care algorithm to identify HIV-infected adolescents at high risk through mother-to-child transmission. This study was published in Tropical Medicine and International Health in 2011. 88. UNICEF, in collaboration with its partners, advocates for and supports effective HIV prevention, treatment, and care for adolescents. Their efforts aim to overcome stigma and discrimination while strengthening national responses to fulfill the rights of vulnerable adolescents.
